title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effectiveness of Upadacitinib in Adolescent Participants with Alopecia Areata
official: A Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study to evaluate efficacy and safety of upadacitinib in pediatric subjects with severe alopecia areata
summary:
Main objective: 1)To assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of upadacitinib compared with placebo for the treatment of signs and symptoms of severe alopecia areata in pediatric subjects.
2) To evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of upadacitinib in extended treatment in pediatric subjects with severe alopecia areata.
3)To evaluate the long-term efficacy, safety, and tolerability of upadacitinib in extended treatment in pediatric subjects with severe alopecia areata.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Eligible subjects will be at least 6 years old at Screening and < 18 years old at Baseline.
2. 2. Eligible subjects must have a diagnosis of severe AA with SALT score ≥ 50 scalp hair loss at Screening and Baseline.
3. 3. Eligible subjects have no spontaneous scalp hair regrowth over the past 6 months.
4. 4. Eligible subjects will have current episode of AA of less than 8 years.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Eligible subjects must not have a current diagnosis of primarily diffuse type of AA.
2. 2. Eligible subjects must not have a diagnosis of other types of alopecia that would interfere with evaluation of AA, including but not limited to female pattern hair loss, male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) Stage III or greater based on Hamilton-Norwood classification, traction alopecia, lichen planopilaris, discoid lupus, frontal fibrosing alopecia, central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia, folliculitis decalvans, trichotillomania, and telogen effluvium.
3. 3. Eligible subjects must not have a diagnosis of other types of inflammatory scalp, eyebrow, or eyelash disorders that would interfere with evaluation of AA, including but not limited to seborrheic dermatitis, scalp psoriasis, AD, and tinea capitis.
